unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 6: LIFE IN THE WORLD

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project about a simple global culinary adventure. In this project, they will pile up a booklet about culinary adventures to explore continents, countries, and food cultures of various regions. They will describe personal food preferences and shopping experiences for specific dietary needs (e.g., vegetarian, gluten-free). Students will create roles based on different countries and act out a shopping experience where they learn about and purchase traditional food from various cultures around the world. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the world with its components such as continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the world'' in English from previous themes and/or years for some countries such as ''Türkiye, England and so on'' some food items such as ''bread, chicken, milk and so on'' and some structures such as ''I have some eggs. I have two apples.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a digital interactive map or a world poster including all counties on it could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss in pairs what the map and the poster include in general and write down what they remember about the topic. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about students’ personal food experiences in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 1: Tasteful Memories The teacher introduces the activity by explaining that students talk about their personal food experiences using the target grammar while focusing on countable and uncountable nouns. Students brainstorm and list 10 food or drink items (a mix of countable and uncountable nouns). They then write five sentences with target grammar about their food experiences (e.g., ''I have eaten beans in a traditional Turkish dish before'', ''I have never tried spicy Korean noodles''.). Later, they pair up to ask and answer questions about their experiences, such as, ''Have you ever eaten sushi?'', ''Yes, I have eaten sushi many times, especially in Japan.''. Finally, the teacher provides constructive feedback on their sentences and interactions. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students differentiate between countable and uncountable nouns by using target vocabulary in English with visual aids and written activities. Activity 1: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns with Visuals The teacher provides students with two sheets of paper. The first sheet contains only pictures of various foods and drinks (e.g., mushrooms, rice, milk). The second sheet is divided into two columns labelled ''Countable Nouns'' and ''Uncountable Nouns'', with a word bank at the top listing the names of the items shown in the pictures. Students first cut out the pictures from the first sheet, then sort and glue them into the correct column on the second sheet. Then, they refer to the word bank to write the appropriate name next to each glued picture (e.g., a picture of mushrooms is glued under ''Countable Nouns'' and ''mushroom'' is written beside it). Students share their completed work for teacher and peer feedback. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
